title: Calendar defaults policy
description: Timezone, operational-day rule, shift template, accounting leaf and holiday treatment used to seed the first `calendar_versions` row of a site and as the fallback when a unit has no published calendar. Spec CAL01 (timezone, operational day start, shift templates, holidays; shifts may cross midnight; production date by operational-day rule; generated UTC boundaries stored), CAL02 (DST handled by the generator, never by this policy), section 3.1 (shift vs daily leaf, never both). Decision D03. Consumed by sub-phase 2.1 (`CalendarService`); the published calendar version, not this policy, is what calculation runs record.

name.description: Label stored on shift instances and periods (e.g. `A`, `Night`).

endLocal.description: endLocal <= startLocal means the shift crosses midnight and ends on the next local date (CAL01); its production date is that of the operational day containing startLocal.

daysOfWeek.description: ISO 8601 weekday numbers of the shift start's local date: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.

timezone.description: Site timezone. Seeding copies `tenants.timezone` when it is a valid IANA id, otherwise `UTC` with a warning flag (2.1 step 1).

operationalDayStart.description: Local time at which the production (operational) day starts; a shift belongs to the operational day containing its start (CAL01).

shiftTemplates.description: Shift pattern per weekday. Templates for the same day must not overlap and should tile the operational day; the calendar generator rejects overlaps when publishing.

accountingLeaf.description: Grain of `production_periods`: one per shift instance, or one per operational day (`shift_name` null). Day and month are roll-ups; shift and day rows are never both counted (section 3.1).

holidayTreatment.description: `excluded`: holiday instances are schedule exclusions (outside S, capacity ledger `schedule_exclusion`). `planned_downtime`: holidays stay inside S as planned availability loss (KPI02).
